Formalization requires expenditure of knowledge: 60 from the home city, 30 from Rail Town, and 30 from Valley, and occupies 1 unit of coordination capacity. The national common law must be operating normally, and the local city and rail transfer station must already be built. The coordination limit supported by basic administration and an administrative archive with normal provisioning must also have room to spare, to prevent an overload shutdown during the transition between administrations.

Rail Town sends 24 parts in exchange for 120 food from Valley. The entire route occupies the home city's original merchant vehicle and two drivers, and cannot depart at the same time as external trade or ferry operations. Each trip expends travel expenses from the home city: 8 food, 2 wood, 0.2 tools, and 0.1 parts.

The empty vehicle takes 90 seconds to reach Rail Town, 150 seconds to carry the parts to Valley, 150 seconds to carry the food back to Rail Town, and 90 seconds to return to the city empty. Time spent waiting for repairs due to blocked roads is added separately. Road merchant vehicles do not benefit from the speed of scheduled railway trains.

Rail Town currently has {变量1} parts; Valley currently has {变量2} food. Both places must first reserve enough for 120 seconds of provisioning and routine maintenance. When goods are unavailable, the merchant vehicle waits there to load. It can be recalled to return the goods before delivery; once delivery is completed, it continues on to Rail Town. The three cities' shared responsibilities

The clinics, schools, fields, and workshops of the three cities have upheld their shared agreement for three consecutive cycles. Convoys on the roads have delivered goods to the warehouses as agreed, and representatives from all three places have gathered with their respective public ledgers.
They are preparing to formally record the shared rights and responsibilities of the cities in a master ledger that this generation and the next can consult at any time.
